title: ALMA Observations of Cold Methanol Gas in the Large Magellanic Cloud: N79 South Giant Molecular Cloud
question: Investigate the physical and chemical properties, molecular abundances, and origin of cold CH$_3$OH gas in two dense molecular cloud cores (N79S-1 and N79S-2) offset from the SSC candidate H72.97-69.39 in the low-metallicity N79 region of the LMC.

data.arrays: 12-m Array (46 antennas for Band 6, 50 antennas for Band 7)
data.sensitivity: Continuum (0.87 mm): 0.158 mJy beam^-1; Line cubes: 135 to 159 mK (Band 6) and 39 to 46 mK (Band 7)

what.value: Coordinates of SSC candidate H72.97-69.39 from Herschel observations

evidence.quote: We observe the massive ($>$ 8 M$_\odot$) YSOs, HSOBMHERICC J72.971176–69.391112 (hereafter H72.97–69.39), located in the N79 South GMC (giant molecular cloud) of the LMC, as identified by Herschel observations (cite: seal14).

what.value: Relative molecular abundances for LMC sources ST11, ST16, N113A1, N105-2A, N105-1C, N105-2E, and N105-3C

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum source sizes and flux densities
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian within the 50% peak intensity contour to measure source sizes, and extract average 0.87 mm continuum flux density within a 0.42'' (0.1 pc) diameter circular region centered on CH3OH peak positions.
key_parameters: 50% peak intensity contour for 2D Gaussian size fit

recipe.goal: Extract spectra, identify molecular transitions, and fit line profiles
recipe.method: Extract spectra from 0.42'' (0.1 pc) diameter regions at CH3OH peaks, identify lines using CASSIS with CDMS and JPL databases (S/N >= 3, matching systemic velocity, unblended), and fit single Gaussian profiles to unblended transitions.
key_parameters: Fitting velocity range: 229 to 236 km s^-1 (N79S-1) and 230 to 238 km s^-1 (N79S-2)

recipe.goal: Create moment zero maps and measure molecular emission source sizes
recipe.method: Integrate spectra over the emission velocity range (typically 229 to 238 km s^-1) to make moment zero maps, and fit 2D Gaussians within the 50% peak intensity region to derive deconvolved source sizes.
key_parameters: Velocity integration range: typically 229 to 238 km s^-1 (205 to 257 km s^-1 for CO(3-2), 205-220 km s^-1 blue lobe, 242-257 km s^-1 red lobe)

recipe.goal: Derive rotational temperatures and column densities of CH3OH and SO, and column densities of other species
recipe.method: Perform LTE rotation diagram analysis (straight-line fit of log(N_u/g_u) vs E_u/k) for CH3OH and SO; validate CH3OH and H2CO with non-LTE RADEX modeling; calculate LTE optically thin column densities for CS, H2CS, H2CO, CN, and CCH by averaging values at T_rot = 10 K and 20 K.
key_parameters: T_rot varied from 10 K to 20 K for CS, H2CS, H2CO, CN, and CCH
RADEX inputs: T_bg = 2.73 K, n(H2) = 1.8e6 cm^-3 (N79S-1) and 3.6e6 cm^-3 (N79S-2), line width = 2.0 km s^-1 (N79S-1) and 2.3 km s^-1 (N79S-2)
assumptions: Gas temperature of 13 K (N79S-1) and 15 K (N79S-2) with 10-20 K bounds for single-transition species

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column densities, gas densities, masses, visual extinctions, and relative molecular abundances
recipe.method: Compute N(H2) from optically thin 0.87 mm dust continuum emission at T_d = 10, 13/15, and 20 K (averaging 10 K and 20 K values as final N(H2)), derive n(H2), gas mass, and A_V assuming a 0.1 pc spherical geometry, and divide molecular column densities by N(H2) to obtain relative abundances.
key_parameters: Dust-to-gas mass ratio Z = 0.0027 and mean atomic mass per hydrogen mu = 1.41
assumptions: Optically thin dust continuum emission and thermal coupling between gas and dust (T_d = 10-20 K)
Spherical gas distribution with 0.1 pc diameter

answer_key.quantity: 0.87 mm continuum peak intensity (SSC continuum peak)
